definition: A symbol that represents a number whose value can change or is not yet known.
example: In 3x + 2, x is the variable. If x = 4, the value is 14.
watch: A letter represents a number; 3x means 3 × x.

definition: One part of an expression separated from the next by addition or subtraction. Keep its sign with it.
example: The terms of 4x² − 3x + 7 are 4x², −3x and 7.
watch: Multiplication inside a term does not split it into separate terms.

definition: The numerical multiplier of a variable or variable part in a term.
example: The coefficient of x in −5x is −5. In x, it is 1.
watch: The coefficient of x in −x is −1, not zero.

The sign belongs to the coefficient."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">−5 × x</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">coefficient = −5</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">The sign belongs to the coefficient.</text></svg>

definition: A fixed number, or a term with no variable in the expression being studied.
example: In 2x² − 3x + 8, the constant term is 8.
watch: The constant is not the same as the coefficient of x.

definition: Terms with exactly the same variable part, including the same powers. Add or subtract their coefficients.
example: 3x² + 5x² = 8x², but 3x² + 5x cannot be combined into one term.
watch: x and x² are different variable parts.

Keep the power."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">3x² + 5x² = 8x²</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">Same variable part: x²</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">Add the coefficients. Keep the power.</text></svg>

definition: A combination of numbers, variables and operations that represents a value. It has no equality statement.
example: 2x + 7 is an expression. It is 13 when x = 3.
watch: An expression can be simplified or evaluated; an equation can be solved.

definition: A statement that two expressions have equal values. Solving finds values that make the statement true.
example: 3x + 2 = 11 has solution x = 3.
watch: Whatever operation you use to preserve equality must be applied to both sides.

Subtract 2 from BOTH sides; divide BOTH by 3."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">3x + 2 = 11</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">3x = 9  →  x = 3</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">Subtract 2 from BOTH sides; divide BOTH by 3.</text></svg>

definition: An equality true for every allowed value of its variable.
example: 2(x + 3) = 2x + 6 is true for every real x.
watch: Checking one value can expose an error, but cannot prove an identity.

Each term inside the brackets is multiplied by 2."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">2(x + 3) = 2x + 6</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">True for every real x</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">Each term inside the brackets is multiplied by 2.</text></svg>

definition: Replacing each occurrence of a variable with a specified value or expression.
example: If x = −2, then x² = (−2)² = 4.
watch: Use brackets around a substituted negative number or expression.

definition: Multiplying through brackets so that every required pair of terms is included.
watch: Two brackets with two terms each create four products before collecting.

Every term in the first bracket meets every term in the second."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">(x + 2)(x + 3)</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">x² + 3x + 2x + 6</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">Every term in the first bracket meets every term in the second.</text></svg>

definition: A number or expression that is multiplied by another to make a product.
example: In (x − 2)(x + 5), the two brackets are factors.
watch: Terms are added; factors are multiplied.

definition: Rewriting an expression as a product of factors. It reverses expansion.
watch: Expand your answer to check it gives the original expression.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="x² + 5x + 6. (x + 2)(x + 3). 2 + 3 = 5 and 2 × 3 = 6."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">x² + 5x + 6</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">(x + 2)(x + 3)</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">2 + 3 = 5 and 2 × 3 = 6.</text></svg>

definition: The greatest shared numerical factor, together with each shared variable to its smallest power.
example: The HCF of 6x² and 9x is 3x, so 6x² + 9x = 3x(2x + 3).
watch: A factor taken outside must divide every term inside.

definition: An expression a² − b², which factorises as (a − b)(a + b).
watch: The identity uses subtraction. a² + b² does not follow this rule over the reals.

definition: A comparison using <, >, ≤ or ≥ instead of equality.
example: −2x < 6 gives x > −3 after dividing by −2.
watch: Multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses the sign.

definition: An equation that can be written ax² + bx + c = 0, with a ≠ 0.
example: x² − 5x + 6 = 0 gives x = 2 or x = 3.
watch: Put the equation equal to zero before applying the zero-product rule.

definition: A value of x that makes an expression or function equal to zero.
example: For f(x) = (x − 2)(x + 3), the roots are 2 and −3.
watch: The roots are x-values. The intercept points are (2, 0) and (−3, 0).

definition: The variable written alone on one side of a formula.
example: From v = u + at, making t the subject gives t = (v − u)/a, with a ≠ 0.
watch: Undo operations in the correct order; keep restrictions on division.

definition: A collection of distinct objects, called elements. Curly brackets list the elements.
example: {2, 4, 6} contains three elements. Repeating 2 does not add a new element.
watch: Order and repetition do not change a set.

definition: An element is one object in a set. The symbol ∈ means belongs to; ∉ means does not belong to.
example: If A = {2, 4, 6}, then 4 ∈ A and 5 ∉ A.
watch: Use ∈ for an element and ⊆ for a subset.

definition: A set whose every element also belongs to another set. A proper subset does not equal that other set.
example: {2, 4} ⊆ {2, 4, 6}. Every set is a subset of itself.
watch: Being a subset does not mean having just one common element.

definition: The set of all objects under consideration in the question. Complements are measured within it.
watch: Changing the universal set can change a complement.

watch: Count an element in both sets only once in their union.

example: If A = {1, 2} and B = {2, 3}, then A ∩ B = {2}.
watch: Intersection means both conditions hold, not either condition.

watch: A complement depends on the chosen universal set.

example: If A = {1, 2} and B = {2, 3}, then A \ B = {1}.
watch: Direction matters: B \ A = {3}, a different set.

example: −3, 0 and 7 are integers; 1.5 is not.
watch: Negative whole numbers are integers too.

definition: A number expressible as a/b where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.
example: 0.75 = 3/4 and 0.333… = 1/3 are rational.
watch: A recurring decimal is rational even though it never ends.

definition: A real number that cannot be written as a ratio of two integers. Its decimal neither terminates nor repeats.
example: √2 and π are irrational.
watch: Not every square root is irrational: √9 = 3.

definition: The exponent tells you the power of a base. For a positive integer exponent, it counts repeated factors.
watch: 2⁴ is not 2 × 4. Add exponents only when multiplying powers with the same base.

For the same base: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">2⁴ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">base = 2; index = 4</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">For the same base: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ.</text></svg>

definition: A negative exponent gives the reciprocal of the corresponding positive power, for a non-zero base.
watch: A negative exponent does not make a positive base give a negative answer.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ   (a ≠ 0). 2⁻³ = 1/8. The reciprocal changes position, not sign."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ   (a ≠ 0)</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">2⁻³ = 1/8</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">The reciprocal changes position, not sign.</text></svg>

definition: For a positive base, a¹⁄ⁿ is its positive nth root, and aᵐ⁄ⁿ = (ⁿ√a)ᵐ.
watch: The denominator gives the root; the numerator gives the power.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="27²⁄³ = (∛27)². 3² = 9. Root first can make the calculation smaller."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">27²⁄³ = (∛27)²</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">3² = 9</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">Root first can make the calculation smaller.</text></svg>

definition: An exact irrational root, often left in radical form instead of rounded to a decimal.
watch: √(a + b) is not generally √a + √b.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="√12 = √(4 × 3) = 2√3. Extract a square factor. 2√3 + 5√3 = 7√3, but √2 + √3 stays separate."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">√12 = √(4 × 3) = 2√3</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">Extract a square factor</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">2√3 + 5√3 = 7√3, but √2 + √3 stays separate.</text></svg>

definition: Writing a non-zero number as a × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ |a| < 10 and n is an integer.
watch: The leading number must have exactly one non-zero digit before its decimal point.

definition: An amount out of one hundred. Divide by 100 to convert a percentage to a decimal.
watch: State what the percentage is OF: the base matters.

definition: The factor that turns an original amount into its new amount after a percentage change.
example: Increase by 12%: multiply by 1.12. Reverse it: divide the new amount by 1.12.
watch: An increase of 20% followed by a decrease of 20% does not restore the original.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="original × 1.12 = new amount. new amount ÷ 1.12 = original. For a decrease of 12%, use 0.88."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">original × 1.12 = new amount</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">new amount ÷ 1.12 = original</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">For a decrease of 12%, use 0.88.</text></svg>

definition: Growth calculated on the updated amount each period, so earlier growth also earns growth.
example: At 5% per year, 200 grows to 200(1.05)³ after three years.
watch: Use the rate and number of periods in matching units.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="200 → 210 → 220.50. Multiply by 1.05 each year. The increase gets bigger because the base grows."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">200 → 210 → 220.50</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">Multiply by 1.05 each year</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">The increase gets bigger because the base grows.</text></svg>

definition: A reduction in value over time, often modelled by repeated percentage decreases.
example: A value of 1,000 falling 10% yearly becomes 1,000(0.9)² = 810 after two years.
watch: Repeated decreases multiply; do not subtract the percentages from the original each time.

definition: Profit expressed as a percentage of cost price.
example: Cost 80, selling price 100: profit 20, so markup = 20/80 × 100% = 25%.
watch: Markup uses cost as its denominator; profit margin uses selling price.

definition: Profit expressed as a percentage of selling price.
example: Cost 80, selling price 100: margin = 20/100 × 100% = 20%.
watch: A 20% margin is not the same as a 20% markup.

definition: Gross pay is pay before deductions. Net pay is the amount left after deductions.
example: Gross 600 less deductions 95 gives net pay 505.
watch: For banded deductions, apply each rate only to the part within its band.

definition: A ratio stating how much one currency is worth in another.
example: At €1 = £0.85, €40 = £34. To turn £34 into euros, divide by 0.85.
watch: Write the units beside the rate so you choose multiplication or division correctly.

definition: The whole group about which a statistical question is being asked.
example: To study all students in a school, the population is every student in that school.
watch: Your population must match the question you want to answer.

definition: The subset of a population from which data is actually collected. Sample size is the number of observations.
example: Surveying 60 students from a school of 800 gives a sample of 60.
watch: A large sample can still be biased if selected unfairly.

definition: A systematic tendency in collection or measurement that favours some answers or groups over others.
example: Asking only rugby players about favourite sports can bias a school-wide survey.
watch: Random selection reduces selection bias; it does not fix a leading question.

definition: Data describing categories or qualities rather than numerical measurements.
example: Favourite colour and type of transport are qualitative.
watch: Using number codes for categories does not make their average meaningful.

definition: Discrete data comes in separate countable values. Continuous data is measured and can take values throughout an interval.
example: Number of siblings is discrete; height is continuous.
watch: Rounding a measurement to whole units does not make the underlying variable discrete.

definition: How many times a value or category occurs in the data.
example: If the value 4 occurs six times, its frequency is 6.
watch: Do not confuse a data value with how often it occurs.

definition: The total of all values divided by the number of values. It represents fair sharing of the total.
watch: An unusually large or small value can strongly affect the mean.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="2 + 4 + 9 = 15. 15 ÷ 3 = 5. Fair share: 5, 5, 5 has the same total."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">2 + 4 + 9 = 15</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">15 ÷ 3 = 5</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">Fair share: 5, 5, 5 has the same total.</text></svg>

definition: The middle value in ordered data. With an even number of values, average the middle two.
example: For 2, 5, 6, 9, the median is (5 + 6)/2 = 5.5.
watch: Order the data first; the middle position is not automatically the median value.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="2,  5,  6,  9. median = (5 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.5. An even-sized list has two middle values."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">2,  5,  6,  9</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">median = (5 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.5</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">An even-sized list has two middle values.</text></svg>

definition: The value or category occurring most often. There may be more than one mode or no unique mode.
example: For 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, the mode is 2.
watch: The mode is the value, not its frequency.

definition: The largest data value minus the smallest. It is a simple measure of spread.
example: For 3, 4, 8, 11, the range is 11 − 3 = 8.
watch: This statistical range is a number; the range of a function is a set of outputs.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="3, 4, 8, 11. range = 11 − 3 = 8. Use the largest and smallest VALUES."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">3, 4, 8, 11</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">range = 11 − 3 = 8</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">Use the largest and smallest VALUES.</text></svg>

definition: A mean where each value contributes according to its weight or frequency: Σfx / Σf.
example: Two scores of 4 and three scores of 6 give mean (2×4 + 3×6)/5 = 5.2.
watch: Divide by total frequency, not the number of distinct values.

definition: A display using separate bars whose heights represent values or frequencies for categories.
example: A bar of height 12 may represent 12 students choosing cycling.
watch: Read the scale; decorative bar width should not change the meaning.

definition: A circle divided into sectors in proportion to category frequencies. The whole circle represents the total.
example: A category with 15 out of 60 values gets (15/60) × 360° = 90°.
watch: Percentages describe shares of the same total.

definition: A display of numerical intervals using adjoining bars. Bar AREA represents frequency.
example: For unequal class widths, use frequency density = frequency ÷ class width as the height.
watch: Equal heights need not mean equal frequencies when widths differ.

definition: A display splitting each value into a stem and a leaf, while retaining the original values.
example: With key 2 | 7 = 27, the row 2 | 1 4 7 means 21, 24, 27.
watch: Always read the key; it determines place value and units.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="2 | 1 4 7. 21, 24, 27. Key: 2 | 7 means 27."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">2 | 1 4 7</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">21, 24, 27</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">Key: 2 | 7 means 27.</text></svg>

definition: Lines in a plane that never meet and remain the same perpendicular distance apart.
example: Distinct lines y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 3 are parallel.
watch: Equal gradients give parallel lines only if the lines are distinct.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Two parallel lines never meet."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><line x1="55" y1="70" x2="425" y2="70" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="55" y1="130" x2="425" y2="130" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3"/><text x="240" y="187" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">Same direction; constant separation.</text></svg>

definition: Lines meeting at a right angle of 90°.
example: A horizontal line and a vertical line are perpendicular.
watch: For two finite, non-zero gradients, perpendicular gradients multiply to −1.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><line x1="65" y1="130" x2="410" y2="130" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="235" y1="20" x2="235" y2="175" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="235" y1="110" x2="255" y2="110" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="255" y1="110" x2="255" y2="130" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="307" y="105" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#173349">90°</text></svg>

definition: The opposite angles made when two straight lines cross. They are equal.
example: If one angle is 68°, the vertically opposite angle is also 68°.
watch: Adjacent angles at the crossing usually differ; those on a straight line sum to 180°.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Opposite angles at a crossing are equal."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><line x1="75" y1="40" x2="405" y2="160" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="75" y1="160" x2="405" y2="40" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" fill="#087f75">68°</text><text x="240" y="147" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="25" fill="#087f75">68°</text><text x="240" y="190" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">Opposite, not next to each other.</text></svg>

definition: Angles occupying matching positions where a transversal crosses two lines. They are equal when those lines are parallel.
example: Matching upper-right angles are equal on two parallel lines.
watch: State the parallel-line condition; the angle positions alone do not guarantee equality.

definition: Angles on opposite sides of a transversal, between two lines. They are equal when those lines are parallel.
example: Equal alternate interior angles can also be used to establish parallel lines.
watch: Identify the two lines and the transversal before choosing the angles.

definition: An angle between one triangle side and the extension of an adjacent side. It equals the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles.
example: If the remote interior angles are 45° and 65°, the exterior angle is 110°.
watch: Do not include the interior angle next to the exterior angle in that sum.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="An exterior triangle angle equals the two remote interior angles."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><polygon points="70,150 175,35 300,150" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="300" y1="150" x2="435" y2="150" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="106" y="137" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">45°</text><text x="181" y="73" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">65°</text><text x="350" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" fill="#3175ba">110°</text></svg>

definition: A triangle with at least two equal sides. The angles opposite those equal sides are equal.
example: If the vertex angle is 40°, each base angle is (180° − 40°)/2 = 70°.
watch: Match an angle to the side opposite it, not the side next to it.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="An isosceles triangle has equal sloping sides and equal base angles."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><polygon points="100,160 240,30 380,160" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="240" y="71" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" fill="#173349">40°</text><text x="149" y="148" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" fill="#087f75">70°</text><text x="331" y="148" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" fill="#087f75">70°</text><text x="240" y="190" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">Equal sides face equal angles.</text></svg>

definition: A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel. Opposite sides and angles are equal; its diagonals bisect each other.
example: A rectangle is a special parallelogram with four right angles.
watch: A general parallelogram need not have equal diagonals or right angles.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel and equal."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><polygon points="70,145 140,45 390,45 320,145" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="70" y1="145" x2="390" y2="45" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="140" y1="45" x2="320" y2="145" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="230" cy="95" r="4" fill="#087f75"/><text x="240" y="185" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">Diagonals cut each other in half.</text></svg>

definition: Figures with the same shape and size. Matching lengths and angles are equal. Triangle tests include SSS, SAS, ASA and right-angle–hypotenuse–side.
example: Two triangles with matching sides 3, 4 and 5 are congruent by SSS.
watch: AAA proves similarity, not congruence; SSA is not a general congruence test.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Two congruent triangles have the same shape and size."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><polygon points="65,145 65,55 170,145" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><polygon points="300,145 300,55 405,145" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="240" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">Matching lengths AND matching angles.</text></svg>

definition: Figures with equal corresponding angles and a common scale factor between corresponding lengths.
example: Sides 3, 4, 5 and 6, 8, 10 form similar triangles with scale factor 2.
watch: Match corresponding sides before forming ratios.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Similar triangles have equal angles and proportional lengths."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><polygon points="40,145 40,95 100,145" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><polygon points="230,145 230,45 350,145" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="73" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">small</text><text x="294" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">twice the lengths</text><text x="180" y="83" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">×2</text></svg>

definition: The multiplier taking an original length to a corresponding new length. Areas scale by k² and volumes by k³.
example: If lengths double, areas multiply by 4 and volumes by 8.
watch: Use the direction requested: new length ÷ original length.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="length × k. area × k²; volume × k³. For k = 2: lengths ×2, areas ×4, volumes ×8."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">length × k</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">area × k²; volume × k³</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">For k = 2: lengths ×2, areas ×4, volumes ×8.</text></svg>

definition: A chain of valid reasons establishing that a statement must be true under its stated assumptions.
example: Using parallel-angle facts and the straight-angle sum can prove a triangle’s angles sum to 180°.
watch: A diagram that looks right or several numerical examples do not by themselves prove a general theorem.

definition: The statement formed by swapping the condition and conclusion of an implication. It needs its own justification.
example: Pythagoras: right triangle implies a² + b² = c². Its converse uses that equality to prove a triangle is right-angled.
watch: The converse of a true statement is not automatically true.

definition: In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: c² = a² + b².
example: A triangle with perpendicular sides 3 and 4 has hypotenuse √(9 + 16) = 5.
watch: This formula needs a right angle. The hypotenuse must be the longest side.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="A right triangle. The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><polygon points="70,155 70,35 330,155" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="70" y1="139" x2="86" y2="139" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="86" y1="139" x2="86" y2="155" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="45" y="100" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" fill="#087f75">3</text><text x="200" y="180" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" fill="#087f75">4</text><text x="220" y="84" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" fill="#3175ba">5</text><text x="379" y="61" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">3² + 4²</text><text x="379" y="93" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">= 5²</text></svg>

definition: A distance measured at right angles to the chosen base or parallel faces.
example: A parallelogram has area base × perpendicular height.
watch: A sloping side is usually not the height.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Height is perpendicular to the base, not the sloping side."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><polygon points="80,145 140,45 400,45 340,145" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="140" y1="45" x2="140" y2="145" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><line x1="140" y1="130" x2="155" y2="130" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="155" y1="130" x2="155" y2="145" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="167" y="101" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#3175ba">h</text><text x="237" y="175" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" fill="#173349">base</text></svg>

definition: A line segment from the centre of a circle or sphere to its boundary, or the length of that segment.
example: A circle of diameter 10 cm has radius 5 cm.
watch: Radius is half the diameter.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Radius of a circle."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="68" fill="none" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="4" fill="#087f75"/><text x="235" y="117" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#173349">O</text><line x1="220" y1="95" x2="288" y2="95" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="4"/><text x="255" y="82" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" fill="#3175ba">r</text><text x="220" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">Radius</text></svg>

definition: A chord through a circle’s centre. Its length is twice the radius.
example: If r = 7, then d = 14.
watch: Using a diameter in a radius formula creates a large error.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Diameter of a circle."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="68" fill="none" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="4" fill="#087f75"/><text x="235" y="117" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#173349">O</text><line x1="152" y1="95" x2="288" y2="95" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="4"/><text x="220" y="77" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#3175ba">d = 2r</text><text x="220" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">Diameter</text></svg>

definition: The distance around a circle: C = 2πr = πd.
example: For radius 3 cm, circumference = 6π cm.
watch: Circumference is a length, so its unit is not cm².
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Circumference of a circle."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="68" fill="none" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="4" fill="#087f75"/><text x="235" y="117" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#173349">O</text><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="68" fill="none" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="369" y="103" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" fill="#173349">C = 2πr</text><text x="220" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">Circumference</text></svg>

definition: A straight line segment joining two points on a circle. A diameter is the longest chord.
example: A chord need not pass through the centre.
watch: A chord is straight; an arc follows the curved boundary.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Chord of a circle."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="68" fill="none" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="4" fill="#087f75"/><text x="235" y="117" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#173349">O</text><line x1="165" y1="135" x2="275" y2="135" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="4"/><text x="220" y="124" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#3175ba">chord</text><text x="220" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">Chord</text></svg>

definition: An arc is part of a circle’s boundary. A sector is the region between two radii and their connecting arc.
example: A 90° sector is one quarter of its circle, so its arc is one quarter of the circumference.
watch: Sector perimeter includes the arc AND the two radii.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Sector of a circle."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="68" fill="none" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="4" fill="#087f75"/><text x="235" y="117" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#173349">O</text><path d="M220 95 L288 95 A68 68 0 0 0 220 27 Z" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="246" y="76" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">90°</text><text x="359" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#173349">¼ of the circle</text><text x="220" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">Sector</text></svg>

definition: A line touching a circle at exactly one point. It is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the touching point.
example: A radius to a tangent point makes a 90° angle with the tangent.
watch: A line cutting the circle at two points is not a tangent.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Tangent of a circle."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="68" fill="none" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="220" cy="95" r="4" fill="#087f75"/><text x="235" y="117" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#173349">O</text><line x1="288" y1="15" x2="288" y2="176" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="220" y1="95" x2="288" y2="95" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="276" y1="95" x2="276" y2="107" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="276" y1="107" x2="288" y2="107" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2"/><text x="361" y="105" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#173349">90°</text><text x="220" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#173349">Tangent</text></svg>

definition: A quadrilateral whose four vertices lie on one circle. Opposite interior angles sum to 180°.
example: If one angle is 108°, the opposite angle is 72°.
watch: The four vertices must lie on the same circle.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="All four vertices of a cyclic quadrilateral lie on one circle."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><circle cx="230" cy="95" r="72" fill="none" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><polygon points="158,95 230,23 302,95 230,167" fill="none" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="191" y="101" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">A</text><text x="272" y="101" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">C</text><text x="385" y="99" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" fill="#173349">A + C</text><text x="385" y="127" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" fill="#173349">= 180°</text></svg>

definition: The total distance around a flat shape. Add the lengths of its exposed boundary edges.
example: A 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle has perimeter 2(7 + 4) = 22 cm.
watch: Internal dividing lines do not count towards the outer perimeter.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Perimeter follows all four outside edges of a rectangle."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="90" y="50" width="300" height="100" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="5"/><text x="240" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" fill="#173349">7 cm</text><text x="439" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="20" fill="#173349">4 cm</text><text x="240" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#173349">P = 7 + 4 + 7 + 4 = 22 cm</text></svg>

definition: The amount of flat surface covered, measured in square units.
example: A rectangle 7 cm long and 4 cm wide has area 28 cm².
watch: Area and perimeter answer different questions.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Area counts square units covering a rectangle."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="120" y="40" width="240" height="120" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><line x1="120" y1="40" x2="120" y2="160" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="40" x2="150" y2="160" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="180" y1="40" x2="180" y2="160" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="210" y1="40" x2="210" y2="160" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="240" y1="40" x2="240" y2="160" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="270" y1="40" x2="270" y2="160" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="300" y1="40" x2="300" y2="160" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="330" y1="40" x2="330" y2="160" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="360" y1="40" x2="360" y2="160" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="120" y1="40" x2="360" y2="40" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="120" y1="70" x2="360" y2="70" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="120" y1="100" x2="360" y2="100" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="120" y1="130" x2="360" y2="130" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="120" y1="160" x2="360" y2="160" stroke="#8bb8ae" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="189" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#173349">8 × 4 = 32 square units</text></svg>

definition: The flat shape revealed by cutting through a solid. A prism has a constant cross-section along its length.
example: Cutting a cylinder perpendicular to its axis gives a circular cross-section.
watch: Volume = cross-sectional area × length requires that area to stay constant.

definition: A solid with the same polygonal cross-section throughout its length, with matching parallel end faces.
example: A triangular prism has volume = area of triangular end × length.
watch: Find the area of one end, not its perimeter.

definition: A solid with two matching parallel circular ends and a constant circular cross-section.
example: A right cylinder has volume πr²h and curved surface area 2πrh.
watch: Total surface area also includes whichever circular ends are present.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="A right cylinder has circular ends of radius r and height h."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><path d="M140 55 L140 145 A90 25 0 0 0 320 145 L320 55" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><ellipse cx="230" cy="55" rx="90" ry="25" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="230" y1="55" x2="320" y2="55" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="275" y="47" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="19" fill="#3175ba">r</text><line x1="350" y1="55" x2="350" y2="145" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="370" y="105" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="23" fill="#3175ba">h</text><text x="230" y="193" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" fill="#173349">V = πr²h</text></svg>

definition: The amount of three-dimensional space a solid occupies, measured in cubic units. Capacity describes how much a container can hold.
example: 1 litre = 1,000 cm³. A 2 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm box has volume 24 cm³.
watch: Convert dimensions before multiplying, or use cubic conversion factors.

definition: The total area of the relevant outside faces or curved surfaces of a solid.
example: A closed cylinder has total surface area 2πrh + 2πr².
watch: An open container may omit a face; read which surfaces are required.

definition: A sphere is perfectly round in three dimensions. A hemisphere is half a sphere.
example: Sphere volume = 4πr³/3. Hemisphere volume = 2πr³/3.
watch: A hemisphere’s total area includes its base: 3πr²; its curved area alone is 2πr².
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="A hemisphere is half a sphere and includes a circular base when total area is requested."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><path d="M100 140 A130 115 0 0 1 360 140 Z" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><ellipse cx="230" cy="140" rx="130" ry="25" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="230" y1="140" x2="360" y2="140" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2"/><text x="294" y="132" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" fill="#3175ba">r</text><text x="230" y="194" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#173349">Curved part + circular base = total area</text></svg>

definition: A number from 0 to 1 measuring how likely an event is. Zero means impossible; one means certain.
example: For a fair die, P(rolling 6) = 1/6.
watch: Probability cannot be negative or exceed 1.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="Probability scale runs from impossible at zero to certain at one."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><line x1="50" y1="95" x2="430" y2="95" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="4"/><circle cx="50" cy="95" r="4" fill="#087f75"/><circle cx="240" cy="95" r="4" fill="#087f75"/><circle cx="430" cy="95" r="4" fill="#087f75"/><text x="50" y="67" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" fill="#173349">0</text><text x="240" y="67" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" fill="#173349">½</text><text x="430" y="67" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="22" fill="#173349">1</text><text x="65" y="137" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#173349">impossible</text><text x="240" y="137" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#173349">even chance</text><text x="417" y="137" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#173349">certain</text></svg>

definition: An outcome is one possible result. An event is a set of outcomes meeting a condition.
example: On a die, 4 is an outcome; “even” is the event {2, 4, 6}.
watch: An event may contain several outcomes.

definition: The set of all possible outcomes of an experiment.
example: Two coin tosses have sample space {HH, HT, TH, TT}.
watch: HT and TH are different ordered outcomes.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="HH   HT   TH   TT. Four ordered outcomes for two tosses. “One head” includes HT and TH."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">HH   HT   TH   TT</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">Four ordered outcomes for two tosses</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">“One head” includes HT and TH.</text></svg>

definition: Outcomes each having the same probability. Only then can simple counting give probability directly.
example: For a fair die, P(even) = 3 favourable outcomes / 6 total outcomes = 1/2.
watch: Do not assume categories such as “win” and “lose” are equally likely.

definition: An event and the event that it does not occur. Their probabilities add to 1.
example: If P(rain) = 0.3, then P(no rain) = 0.7 in the stated model.
watch: The complement covers every outcome outside the event.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="P(not A) = 1 − P(A). 0.7 + 0.3 = 1. Together, the event and its complement cover all outcomes."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">P(not A) = 1 − P(A)</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">0.7 + 0.3 = 1</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">Together, the event and its complement cover all outcomes.</text></svg>

definition: Events for which knowing that one happened does not change the probability of the other.
example: Two tosses of a fair coin are independent: P(H then H) = 1/2 × 1/2.
watch: Drawing without replacement usually changes the next probability.

definition: A branching diagram listing successive outcomes. Multiply along a path; add probabilities of distinct paths forming the event.
example: With 3 red and 2 blue balls, P(two red without replacement) = 3/5 × 2/4.
watch: Update the remaining counts after a draw without replacement.

definition: The number of times an event occurs divided by the total number of trials. It estimates probability.
example: If a result occurs 18 times in 50 trials, its relative frequency is 18/50 = 0.36.
watch: An experimental estimate need not equal the theoretical probability exactly.

definition: An ordered pair locating a point: x gives its horizontal position, y its vertical position.
example: (3, −2) means 3 units right and 2 units down from the origin.
watch: (3, −2) and (−2, 3) usually name different points.

definition: The point halfway along a segment. Average the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates separately.
example: The midpoint of (2, 1) and (8, 5) is (5, 3).
watch: Midpoint coordinates are averages, not coordinate differences.

definition: The change in y divided by the corresponding change in x: m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁).
example: A rise of 2 over a run of 5 gives gradient 2/5.
watch: Vertical lines have undefined gradient because the horizontal change is zero.

definition: A point where a graph meets an axis. At the x-axis y = 0; at the y-axis x = 0.
example: For y = 2x + 6, the intercepts are (−3, 0) and (0, 6).
watch: An intercept point has two coordinates; an intercept value is just one number.

definition: Equations that must hold for the same values of the unknowns. Their shared solution satisfies every equation.
example: x + y = 7 and x − y = 1 give x = 4 and y = 3.
watch: Check both values in both original equations.

definition: The straight-line distance between (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂): √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²).
example: From (1, 2) to (4, 6), the horizontal and vertical changes are 3 and 4, so distance is 5.
watch: Do not add the horizontal and vertical changes unless the route actually follows those two segments.

definition: A comparison of quantities using the same units. A ratio a:b describes relative parts.
example: Sharing 60 in the ratio 2:3 gives 5 parts, 12 per part, so shares 24 and 36.
watch: The first share is 2/5 of the total, not 2/3.

definition: Distance travelled per unit time. Average speed equals total distance divided by total elapsed time.
example: 90 km in 1.5 hours gives average speed 60 km/h.
watch: For a whole journey, include stops in elapsed time if the question includes them.

definition: A relationship y = kx with a constant ratio y/x for non-zero x. Its graph is a straight line through the origin.
example: At a fixed €3 per item with no fixed fee, cost C = 3n.
watch: A straight line with a non-zero intercept does not show direct proportion.

definition: An ordered list of terms following a stated or inferred rule.
example: 4, 7, 10, 13, … is a sequence with an increase of 3 each step.
watch: A few starting values alone may fit more than one possible rule.

definition: A formula giving a sequence’s value from its position n. The position is the input, not the term value.
example: For Tₙ = 3n + 1, the tenth term is T₁₀ = 31.
watch: Check whether the sequence starts at n = 0 or n = 1.

Position and value are different.</text></svg>

definition: A sequence with a constant difference between consecutive terms. For first position 1, Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d.
example: 5, 9, 13, 17 has first term 5 and difference 4, so Tₙ = 4n + 1.
watch: There are n − 1 jumps from the first term to the nth term.

definition: A sequence described by Tₙ = an² + bn + c with a ≠ 0. Its second differences are constant and equal to 2a.
example: 1, 4, 9, 16 has first differences 3, 5, 7 and second differences 2, 2.
watch: Constant first differences indicate a linear rule, not a quadratic one.

definition: A rule assigning exactly one output to every allowed input. Different inputs may share an output.
example: For f(x) = x², both −2 and 2 give output 4; this is still a function.
watch: One input giving two different outputs fails the function rule.

definition: The set of inputs for which a function is defined in the stated problem.
example: For f(x) = 1/x over the reals, x = 0 must be excluded from the domain.
watch: A formula alone may not specify the whole domain; also read the stated restrictions.

example: For x² with domain {−1, 0, 1} and codomain {0, 1, 4}, the value 4 is allowed but not reached.
watch: Codomain and range need not be equal.

definition: The set of outputs actually produced by inputs in the domain.
example: For x² on {−1, 0, 1}, the range is {0, 1}.
watch: This is a set of outputs, not largest minus smallest.

definition: A function that reverses the input–output mapping. It exists on the reached outputs when each output identifies exactly one original input.
example: If f(x) = 3x + 2 on the reals, f⁻¹(y) = (y − 2)/3.
watch: x² on all real numbers has no inverse function unless its domain is restricted.

definition: The side opposite the right angle in a right triangle. It is the longest side.
example: In a 3–4–5 right triangle, the hypotenuse is 5.
watch: Its identity does not depend on which acute angle you choose.

definition: For a chosen acute angle in a right triangle, the opposite side faces it; the adjacent side touches it and is not the hypotenuse.
example: Changing the chosen acute angle swaps the opposite and adjacent legs.
watch: Label the right angle, hypotenuse and reference angle before choosing a ratio.

definition: In a right triangle: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite/adjacent.
example: If opposite = 3 and hypotenuse = 5, then sin θ = 3/5.
watch: These side ratios apply to right triangles; match the ratio to the sides you know.

definition: A calculator operation used to find an angle from a trigonometric ratio.
example: If sin θ = 0.6 for an acute angle, θ = sin⁻¹(0.6) ≈ 36.9°.
watch: sin⁻¹ is not 1/sin. Use degree mode when the required answer is in degrees.

definition: An angle of elevation is measured upward from a horizontal line; an angle of depression is measured downward from it.
example: For an observer looking up, tan θ = vertical rise / horizontal distance.
watch: Add the observer’s eye height if the question asks for total object height.

definition: A function of the form y = mx + c. The gradient m is constant and c is the y-intercept.
example: For y = 2x − 3, each increase of 1 in x raises y by 2.
watch: A linear function can decrease if its gradient is negative.

definition: The curved graph of a quadratic function y = ax² + bx + c, with a ≠ 0.
example: If a > 0 it opens upward; if a < 0 it opens downward.
watch: A parabola need not cross the x-axis twice; it can touch once or not meet it.

definition: A point where a graph changes from decreasing to increasing or vice versa. A quadratic has one turning point.
example: For y = (x − 2)² + 3, the turning point is (2, 3), a minimum.
watch: A turning point is a coordinate pair, not just a maximum or minimum value.

definition: A function with the variable in the exponent, such as y = aˣ where a > 0 and a ≠ 1.
example: For y = 2ˣ, increasing x by 1 doubles y. For y = (1/2)ˣ, it halves y.
watch: Equal input steps give equal multiplying factors, not equal additions.

definition: A graph showing a distance or position against time. On a distance-travelled graph, gradient represents speed.
example: A horizontal section means the plotted distance is not changing during that time.
watch: Read the vertical-axis wording: distance from home can decrease, but cumulative distance travelled cannot.

definition: Moving every point by the same directed distance, without turning or reflecting the figure.
example: The move (3, −2) takes (1, 5) to (4, 3).
watch: State both direction and distance, or give the movement vector.

definition: Mapping a point across a mirror line so that the line perpendicularly bisects the segment joining the point and its image.
example: Reflection in the y-axis takes (3, 2) to (−3, 2).
watch: Points on the mirror line stay fixed.

definition: Turning a figure through an angle about a fixed centre. Specify the centre, angle and direction.
example: A 90° anticlockwise rotation about the origin takes (2, 1) to (−1, 2).
watch: Rotating about a different centre usually gives a different image.

definition: A figure has axial symmetry if reflection in a line maps it onto itself. That line is an axis of symmetry.
example: A non-square rectangle has two axes of symmetry.
watch: A diagonal of a non-square rectangle is not an axis of symmetry.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="A rectangle has horizontal and vertical axes of symmetry."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="80" y="45" width="320" height="115" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="240" y1="20" x2="240" y2="180" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><line x1="50" y1="102.5" x2="430" y2="102.5" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><text x="240" y="195" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">Two mirror lines for a non-square rectangle.</text></svg>

definition: A figure has central symmetry about a point when a 180° rotation about that point maps it onto itself.
example: A parallelogram has central symmetry about the intersection of its diagonals.
watch: Central symmetry need not imply any line of symmetry.

definition: A line passing through the midpoint of a segment at 90°. Every point on it is equally distant from the segment’s endpoints.
example: Intersect equal-radius arcs from A and B, then join the two arc intersections.
watch: The arc radius must be greater than half AB so the arcs cross twice.

definition: A ray or line dividing an angle into two equal angles.
example: Bisecting a 70° angle creates two 35° angles.
watch: Do not split a measured side in half and assume the angle is bisected.

definition: A drawing made using specified geometric tools and justified steps, usually a straightedge and compass.
example: To construct a triangle from three side lengths, draw one side and intersect arcs for the other two lengths.
watch: Keep construction arcs visible when they show the required method.

definition: The included angle is the angle between two stated sides. An included side lies between two stated angles.
example: In a SAS triangle construction, draw the given angle, then mark the two side lengths along its arms.
watch: An angle elsewhere in the triangle is not the included angle.

definition: The number of distinct elements in a finite set.
watch: A set containing zero has one element: n({0}) = 1, while n(∅) = 0.

definition: Digits counted from the first non-zero digit when expressing a value to a chosen precision.
example: 0.004786 to three significant figures is 0.00479.
watch: Leading zeros set place value but do not count as significant figures.

definition: For any non-zero base a, a⁰ = 1.
watch: The rule requires a ≠ 0; do not use it to decide 0⁰.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 200" role="img" aria-label="a³ ÷ a³ = 1. a³⁻³ = a⁰ = 1. The base must be non-zero."><rect width="480" height="200" rx="12" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="22" width="430" height="65" rx="8" fill="#e8f5f1"/><text x="240" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#087f75">a³ ÷ a³ = 1</text><text x="240" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="21" fill="#173349">a³⁻³ = a⁰ = 1</text><text x="240" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#173349">The base must be non-zero.</text></svg>

definition: A fraction whose numerator or denominator contains an algebraic expression. Denominators must not be zero.
example: (x² − 4)/(x − 2) = x + 2 only for x ≠ 2.

definition: Frequency divided by class width. It is the histogram height when bar area must represent frequency.
example: A class of width 5 containing 20 values has density 20/5 = 4.
watch: Read whether the vertical axis shows frequency or frequency density.

definition: A mean estimated by treating every value in a class as equal to that class’s midpoint: Σ(f × midpoint)/Σf.
example: For a class from 10 to 20, use midpoint 15 in the weighted calculation.
watch: The result is an estimate because the exact values within each class are unknown.

definition: A sequence formed by multiplying each term by the same constant ratio. For first position 1, Tₙ = arⁿ⁻¹.
example: 3, 6, 12, 24 has first term 3 and ratio 2, so Tₙ = 3 × 2ⁿ⁻¹.
watch: A common ratio is a multiplier; a common difference is an addition.

definition: For the same arc, the angle at the centre is twice an angle at the circumference standing on that arc.
example: A circumference angle of 35° corresponds to a centre angle of 70° on the same arc.
watch: Check which arc is used; the relevant centre angle may be reflex.
